Create output directory for visualizations os.makedirs('profiling_results', exist_ok=True) def profile_column(conn, table_name, column_name): """Profile a single column with all required analyses""" profile = {} # Get column data type type_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table_name});" columns = pd.read_sql(type_query, conn) col_info = columns[columns['name'] == column_name].iloc[0] data_type = col_info['type'] # Get sample data sample_query = f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name} LIMIT 10000;" data_sample = pd.read_sql(sample_query, conn) # Basic info profile['column_name'] = column_name profile['data_type'] = data_type profile['sample_values'] = data_sample[column_name].head(5).tolist() # Missing values missing_count = data_sample[column_name].isna().sum() profile['missing_count'] = missing_count profile['missing_pct'] = round(missing_count/len(data_sample)*100, 2) # Uniqueness unique_count = data_sample[column_name].nunique() profile['unique_count'] = unique_count profile['uniqueness_ratio'] = round(unique_count/len(data_sample), 4) # Numeric analysis if data_type in ('INTEGER', 'REAL'): # Distribution stats numeric_data = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name};", conn) profile['numeric_stats'] = numeric_data.describe().to_dict() # Skewness and kurtosis skew = stats.skew(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) kurt = stats.kurtosis(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) profile['skewness'] = round(skew, 4) profile['kurtosis'] = round(kurt, 4) # Outlier detection # IQR method Q1 = numeric_data[column_name].quantile(0.25) Q3 = numeric_data[column_name].quantile(0.75) IQR = Q3 - Q1 iqr_outliers = numeric_data[(numeric_data[column_name] < (Q1 - 1.5*IQR)) | (numeric_data[column_name] > (Q3 + 1.5*IQR))] profile['iqr_outliers_count'] = len(iqr_outliers) # Z-score method z_scores = stats.zscore(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) z_outliers = np.sum(np.abs(z_scores) > 3) profile['zscore_outliers_count'] = z_outliers # Isolation Forest iso = IsolationForest(contamination=0.05) iso_pred = iso.fit_predict(numeric_data[column_name].values.reshape(-1, 1)) iso_outliers = sum(iso_pred == -1) profile['isolation_forest_outliers_count'] = iso_outliers return profile # Profile each column (excluding ID fields) profiles = [] for col in column_names: if 'id' not in col.lower(): # Skip ID fields print(f"Profiling {col}...") profile = profile_column(conn, target_table, col) profiles.append(profile) # import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from scipy import stats
import seaborn as sns
import os

# Create output directory for visualizations
os.makedirs('profiling_results', exist_ok=True)

def profile_column(conn, table_name, column_name):
    """Profile a single column with all required analyses"""
    profile = {}
    
    # Get column data type
    type_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table_name});"
    columns = pd.read_sql(type_query, conn)
    col_info = columns[columns['name'] == column_name].iloc[0]
    data_type = col_info['type']
    
    # Get sample data
    sample_query = f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name} LIMIT 10000;"
    data_sample = pd.read_sql(sample_query, conn)
    
    # Basic info
    profile['column_name'] = column_name
    profile['data_type'] = data_type
    profile['sample_values'] = data_sample[column_name].head(5).tolist()
    
    # Missing values
    missing_count = data_sample[column_name].isna().sum()
    profile['missing_count'] = missing_count
    profile['missing_pct'] = round(missing_count/len(data_sample)*100, 2)
    
    # Uniqueness
    unique_count = data_sample[column_name].nunique()
    profile['unique_count'] = unique_count
    profile['uniqueness_ratio'] = round(unique_count/len(data_sample), 4)
    
    # Top frequent values (for non-ID fields)
    if 'id' not in column_name.lower() and data_type not in ('TEXT', 'INTEGER'):
        top_values = data_sample[column_name].value_counts().head(20)
        profile['top_values'] = top_values.to_dict()
    
    # Numeric analysis
    if data_type in ('INTEGER', 'REAL'):
        # Distribution stats
        numeric_data = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name};", conn)
        profile['numeric_stats'] = numeric_data.describe().to_dict()
        
        # Histogram
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
        sns.histplot(numeric_data[column_name], kde=True)
        plt.title(f'Distribution of {column_name}')
        plt.savefig(f'profiling_results/{column_name}_histogram.png')
        plt.close()
        
        # Skewness and kurtosis
        skew = stats.skew(numeric_data[column_name].dropna())
        kurt = stats.kurtosis(numeric_data[column_name].dropna())
        profile['skewness'] = round(skew, 4)
        profile['kurtosis'] = round(kurt, 4)
        
        # Outlier detection
        # IQR method
        Q1 = numeric_data[column_name].quantile(0.25)

    if isinstance(obj, (np.integer, np.floating)):

    elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
        return obj.tolist()
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):

    elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [convert_numpy_types(x) for x in obj]
    return obj

def profile_column(conn, table_name, column_name):
    """Profile a single column with all required analyses"""
    profile = {}
    
    # Get column data type
    type_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table_name});"
    columns = pd.read_sql(type_query, conn)
    col_info = columns[columns['name'] == column_name].iloc[0]
    data_type = col_info['type']
    
    # Get sample data
    sample_query = f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name} LIMIT 10000;"
    data_sample = pd.read_sql(sample_query, conn)
    
    # Basic info
    profile['column_name'] = column_name
    profile['data_type'] = data_type
    profile['sample_values'] = data_sample[column_name].head(5).tolist()
    
    # Missing values
    missing_count = data_sample[column_name].isna().sum()
    profile['missing_count'] = int(missing_count)
    profile['missing_pct'] = round(missing_count/len(data_sample)*100, 2)
    
    # Uniqueness
    unique_count = data_sample[column_name].nunique()
    profile['unique_count'] = int(unique_count)
    profile['uniqueness_ratio'] = round(unique_count/len(data_sample), 4)
    
    # Top frequent values (for non-ID fields)
    if 'id' not in column_name.lower() and data_type not in ('TEXT', 'INTEGER'):
        top_values = data_sample[column_name].value_counts().head(20)
        profile['top_values'] = convert_numpy_types(top_values.to_dict())
    
    # Numeric analysis
    if data_type in ('INTEGER', 'REAL'):
        # Distribution stats
        numeric_data = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name};", conn)
        profile['numeric_stats'] = convert_numpy_types(numeric_data.describe().to_dict())
        
        # Histogram
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
        sns.histplot(numeric_data[column_name], kde=True)

        plt.close()
        
        # Skewness and kurtosis
        skew = stats.skew(numeric_data[column_name].dropna())
        kurt = stats.kurtosis(numeric_data[column_name].dropna())
        profile['skewness'] = float(skew)
        profile['kurtosis'] = float(kurt)

        z_outliers = np.sum(np.abs(z_scores) > 3)
        profile['zscore_outliers_count'] = int(z_outliers)
        
        # Isolation Forest
        iso = IsolationForest(contamination=0.05)
        iso_pred = iso.fit_predict(numeric_data[column_name].values.reshape(-1, 1))
        iso_outliers = sum(iso_pred == -1)
        profile['isolation_forest_outliers_count'] = int(iso_outliers)
    
    return profile

Processes all columns systematically We'll start with the profiling function implementation. ```python import sqlite3 import pandas as pd import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest from scipy import stats import seaborn as sns import os # Create output directory for visualizations os.makedirs('profiling_results', exist_ok=True) def profile_column(conn, table_name, column_name): """Profile a single column with all required analyses""" profile = {} # Get column data type type_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table_name});" columns = pd.read_sql(type_query, conn) col_info = columns[columns['name'] == column_name].iloc[0] data_type = col_info['type'] # Get sample data sample_query = f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name} LIMIT 10000;" data_sample = pd.read_sql(sample_query, conn) # Basic info profile['column_name'] = column_name profile['data_type'] = data_type profile['sample_values'] = data_sample[column_name].head(5).tolist() # Missing values missing_count = data_sample[column_name].isna().sum() profile['missing_count'] = missing_count profile['missing_pct'] = round(missing_count/len(data_sample)*100, 2) # Uniqueness unique_count = data_sample[column_name].nunique() profile['unique_count'] = unique_count profile['uniqueness_ratio'] = round(unique_count/len(data_sample), 4) # Top frequent values (for non-ID fields) if 'id' not in column_name.lower() and data_type not in ('TEXT', 'INTEGER'): top_values = data_sample[column_name].value_counts().head(20) profile['top_values'] = top_values.to_dict() # Numeric analysis if data_type in ('INTEGER', 'REAL'): # Distribution stats numeric_data = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT {column_name} FROM {table_name};", conn) profile['numeric_stats'] = numeric_data.describe().to_dict() # Histogram plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) sns.histplot(numeric_data[column_name], kde=True) plt.title(f'Distribution of {column_name}') plt.savefig(f'profiling_results/{column_name}_histogram.png') plt.close() # Skewness and kurtosis skew = stats.skew(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) kurt = stats.kurtosis(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) profile['skewness'] = round(skew, 4) profile['kurtosis'] = round(kurt, 4) # Outlier detection # IQR method Q1 = numeric_data[column_name].quantile(0.25) Q3 = numeric_data[column_name].quantile(0.75) IQR = Q3 - Q1 iqr_outliers = numeric_data[(numeric_data[column_name] < (Q1 - 1.5*IQR)) | (numeric_data[column_name] > (Q3 + 1.5*IQR))] profile['iqr_outliers_count'] = len(iqr_outliers) # Z-score method z_scores = stats.zscore(numeric_data[column_name].dropna()) z_outliers = np.sum(np.abs(z_scores) > 3) profile['zscore_outliers_count'] = z_outliers # Isolation Forest iso = IsolationForest(contamination=0.05) iso_pred = iso.fit_predict(numeric_data[column_name].values.reshape(-1, 1)) iso_outliers = sum(iso_pred == -1) profile['isolation_forest_outliers_count'] = iso_outliers return profile # Connect to database and profile all columns conn = sqlite3.connect('dacomp-055.sqlite') target_table = 'customer360__customer_value_analysis' # Get all column names columns_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({target_table});" columns = pd.read_sql(columns_query, conn) column_names = columns['name'].tolist() # Profile each column (excluding ID fields) profiles = [] for col in column_names: if 'id' not in col.lower(): # Skip ID fields print(f"Profiling {col}...") profile = profile_column(conn, target_table, col) profiles.append(profile) # Save all profiles to JSON import json with open('profiling_results/full_profile.json', 'w') as f: json.dump(profiles, f, indent=2) conn.close() print("Profiling complete.
